observation.visible_scene: View from inside a moving car, framed on the driver-side (left) wing mirror and the adjacent window. The mirror's reflection shows the roadway behind: a dark SUV/truck with lit headlights following, distant traffic signals, low commercial buildings, and a bright low-sky glow. The window shows the roadside scenery (red-brick building, then a green house) and, separately, a silver SUV seen directly through the glass.
visible_changes: Roadside buildings seen through the window translate steadily toward the left edge of frame (red-brick building exits left, green house enters from left then also drifts left), consistent with the host car moving forward.

A silver SUV appears at the upper-right of the window around t=1.0s and moves leftward across the window view, exiting the left side by about t=2.1s; this is a directly-seen vehicle, not the mirror reflection.
The dark following vehicle in the mirror stays roughly centered and similar in size throughout the excerpt, with only minor positional jitter; no clear approach or recession is established.

The mirror housing, A-pillar, and door panel remain in approximately the same screen position, with small handheld-style shifts, indicating the camera is fixed relative to the car interior rather than panning across it.
outside_clip_unknowns: The host car's exact speed, lane changes, or turns before and after this cropped segment.
Whether the following vehicle in the mirror is closing distance or maintaining it (no onset/completion of any maneuver is shown).
The relationship between the silver SUV in the window and the host car (oncoming vs. passing) is not determined by the clip alone.
uncertain_details: Small frame-to-frame wobble of the mirror/door is likely camera handheld jitter and/or road vibration, not deliberate camera motion; direction of any true camera pan is uncertain.
Subtle changes in the size/position of the mirror-reflected SUV are within noise and should not be read as definite relative motion.
